fatal_errors: The proposed method is selective dealloying, whereas the target method is spray-drying followed by hydrogen thermal decomposition-reduction at approximately 300°C.
The hypothesis assumes a preformed homogeneous alloy containing sacrificial elements; the target begins with spray-dried, compositionally uniform mixed-salt precursor particles.

The proposed framework forms through selective dissolution and noble-metal enrichment, while the target framework forms through sequential reduction, hydrogen spillover-assisted incorporation of transition metals, and solid-solution alloying without sacrificial-element removal.
The suggested acidic/basic electrochemical processing conditions do not match the target hydrogen reduction and thermal phase-tuning conditions.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goal of producing porous NM-HEA three-dimensional frameworks and gives a scientifically plausible dealloying route with sensible limitations and a falsifiable characterization plan. However, it does not reconstruct the reported SD-TDR synthesis, precursor state, hydrogen-assisted reduction mechanism, Pt/Ir/Ru seeding behavior, or fcc-to-hcp phase control. Its catalytic prediction is only generic and does not identify methanol oxidation, Pt black as the benchmark, or the reported activity and surface-area gains. With no cited evidence, it should be treated as a plausible alternative rather than an evidence-supported reconstruction of the target work.
